facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Concentration among distributors is rising and is, in our view, the largest business risk. Experian, TransUnion and Equifax together paid 63% of third-quarter revenue, up from 51% in fiscal 2025 and 41% in fiscal 2023, and they established VantageScore, a joint venture that sells a competing score. These distributors can ask to change the terms on which they offer the FICO Score, and the company says it has limited visibility until their royalty reports arrive, so a change in one relationship would reach the highest-margin revenue first. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 53

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Growth in Scores leans on price, which can reverse. The company attributes the third-quarter business-to-business increase to a higher mortgage origination scores unit price, its risk factors warn that limits on score fees could constrain further price increases, and the Federal Housing Finance Agency director announced in July 2025 that mortgage originators may choose the credit score they submit to Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac. A price or policy reversal would fall almost directly to profit because the segment's costs are small, which is our interpretation of its 91% third-quarter margin. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is cash generation and market access. Free cash flow was USD 750.04 million in nine months, the Scores margin reached 91% in the third quarter, capital spending is light, and the company placed USD 1.5 billion of senior notes in May 2025 and USD 1.0 billion in March 2026 while the disclosed fair value of its senior notes was 98.04% of face value on 2026-06-30. The revolving line runs to 2030-05-13, covenant compliance is reported, no cash dividend has been paid since May 2017, and the filings record no priming, uptier or other action against existing lenders. Repurchase programmes are open-ended authorisations, not commitments, so the board can slow them at any time; only the accelerated repurchase is contractually fixed. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-07-29_exhibit991erq32026.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 61; calculation CALC-06

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: Risk would fall if the board commits repurchases to free cash flow, states a leverage target, or the proxy statement shows a stable holder base and independent oversight of financial policy. It would rise if repurchases again exceed free cash flow after the covenant ceiling steps down to 4.0x on 2026-12-31, if the board starts a further programme funded by borrowing, if a consumer reporting agency or the federal housing regulator changes how the FICO Score is priced or used in mortgages, or if the antitrust claim produces a remedy that touches score pricing. facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: In fiscal 2026 the company took two large financing steps. On 2026-03-20 it issued USD 1.0 billion of 6.25% senior notes due 2034 and used the proceeds to make a payment against the revolving line and to repay in full, before its May 2026 maturity, the USD 400.0 million 5.25% notes. On 2026-06-05 it borrowed a USD 1.5 billion unsecured term loan maturing 2028-05-15 under an amended credit agreement and paid USD 1.5 billion the same day to Wells Fargo Securities under an accelerated share repurchase, receiving an initial 1,055,103 shares worth about USD 1.2 billion and prepaying USD 300.0 million for shares to be delivered when the agreement settles, expected in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026. facts.label: Revenue durability and pricing power
facts.text: Revenue is recurring in Software and usage-based in Scores, and neither is locked in for a creditor's horizon. Software recurring revenue was USD 815.8 million at 2026-06-30 and remaining performance obligations were USD 680.4 million, about half due within 14 months, which gives visibility. Scores royalties give none because distributors report volumes after the period. Pricing power is evident, since the third-quarter business-to-business increase was attributed to a higher mortgage origination scores unit price, but three consumer reporting agencies paid 63% of quarterly revenue, they sell a competing score, and the company's own risk factors say fee limits or a regulator's score-choice decision could constrain price. Price, concentration and policy risk are one risk, so revenue is predictable in Software and cyclical, concentrated and exposed to substitution in Scores. facts.label: Margin resilience and cost flexibility
facts.text: Margins are high and hard to erode through costs but can fall sharply on revenue. Scores segment costs were 10% of segment revenue for nine months, so lost price or volume falls almost entirely to operating income, while Software segment margin fell to 28% from 31% as point-in-time licence sales declined and third-party hosting costs rose. Operating expenses were 47% of revenue, with personnel and hosting the main increases, and 226 positions were removed in fiscal 2025, so cost action is available. Margins can be defended against modest volume pressure but not against a loss of Scores price. facts.label: Industry forces
facts.text: Rivalry is intense in Software and concentrated in Scores. In Software the company names fraud, origination and decisioning competitors such as Nice Actimize, Experian, Pegasystems and SAS and says many competitors are larger. In Scores the one scaled rival is VantageScore, a joint venture of the same three agencies that distribute the FICO Score. Entry is hard because the company holds no consumer credit data of its own and scores are built on agency files, but the housing regulator's validation process lets lenders use other models. Substitutes are in-house models and alternative scores, so price is the lever that most invites substitution, which is an analyst interpretation. facts.label: Regulatory and macro factors
facts.text: Regulatory and economic factors are material to credit, while social and technology factors are not a primary driver on the supplied materials. Use of the FICO Score for mortgages sold to Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac is subject to ongoing validation by those enterprises and their regulator, whose director announced in July 2025 that originators may choose the credit score they submit, and legislative or regulatory limits on score fees could constrain price increases. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The issuer-specific downside begins with a pricing or policy event in mortgage scores, for example score choice moving volume to a competing score or a distributor winning a lower price. The first operational break is Scores revenue: segment costs are small, so the nine-month increase in Scores segment operating income of USD 363.76 million would reverse almost one for one, taking derived EBITDA from USD 1,252.44 million to USD 888.68 million. Derived gross leverage would reach 6.28x, net leverage 6.00x and, even if share-based compensation of USD 174.29 million were added back, 5.25x, against stated ceilings of 4.5x, 4.0x and 3.5x. A reversal of only half the increase gives 5.21x. facts.text: Liquidity is the second step and holds. After run-rate interest of USD 316.51 million, tax at the nine-month rate and capital spending, about USD 400.83 million of cash would remain against USD 300.00 million of term loan installments, with USD 290.00 million of undrawn revolver and repurchases as a lever. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid a liquidity crisis, but a covenant test on a definition not supplied would be the first constraint, and an amendment of the kind agreed in June 2026 could be needed before the ceiling falls to 4.0x. This is an illustration of mechanics, not a forecast or a default view. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Fair Isaac presents a strong business profile supported by a 90% Scores margin and free cash flow of USD 960.88 million, but credit quality is constrained by derived gross leverage of 4.46x built through borrowing-funded repurchases. Cash-flow durability appears adequate: conversion is high, but it depends on mortgage score price and three distributors. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on repurchases slowing, on the covenant definition and on continued market access before the fiscal 2028 maturities of USD 1,987.50 million. The primary downside path is a pricing or policy change that reduces Scores earnings while interest and the covenant ceiling tighten. Against typical leveraged-credit issuers the profile is stronger on margin and cash conversion and weaker on leverage, but that comparison is qualitative because no peer data is supplied. Further analysis would require the executed credit agreement, the price and volume split of Scores growth and market evidence. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: borrowing-funded repurchases against a concentrated earnings base. ## Findings
### Bottom line

The supplied filings and releases support the financial, business and fundamental credit work for FAIR ISAAC CORP through June 2026, but covenant headroom cannot be tested because no executed credit agreement or indenture was supplied, so creditors cannot confirm the covenant cushion. The leverage covenant steps down in stages through 2027, so the missing definition of its earnings measure bears directly on that cushion.

The latest evidence is the third-quarter fiscal 2026 report, 99 days before the as-of date, so the fiscal year-end position, the settlement of the accelerated share repurchase and any later financing are not established. The 2026 debt additions also make the annual report's obligations table out of date, and ratings, debt prices, peer data and the proxy statement with board and ownership detail were not supplied, which limits governance and relative-value work rather than the core credit analysis.

## Request

FAIR ISAAC CORP (issuer id fico), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway: normalise the issuer's statements for fiscal 2023 to fiscal 2025 and the first three quarters of fiscal 2026, build net debt, leverage, coverage and liquidity tables, and state the definitions and gaps that limit them.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Debt-funded repurchases lifted derived gross leverage to 4.46x last-twelve-months EBITDA from 3.25x at the 2025 year-end, so creditors now rely on Scores earnings to service USD 2,526.70 million more debt. A USD 1,500.00 million accelerated share repurchase in June 2026 was funded by a new term loan of the same size.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 10–12; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-05; calculation CALC-06; calculation CALC-12

Operating strength is intact, with last-twelve-months EBITDA of USD 1,252.44 million and cash interest cover of 7.60x, but that cover rests on interest paid before the new term loan and notes had run for a full year. The issuer reports no EBITDA, so every EBITDA figure here is derived from operating income and depreciation and amortization, and the covenant's own definition, which is not printed, may give a different ratio.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 2–5; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; calculation CALC-02; calculation CALC-03; calculation CALC-07
### Leverage and coverage

Derived gross leverage was 2.96x at the 2024 year-end, 3.25x at the 2025 year-end and 4.46x at 2026-06-30, with net leverage of 2.75x, 3.11x and 4.26x. The step-up in the third quarter of fiscal 2026 comes from the debt side: gross debt at carrying value rose by USD 2,526.70 million between the 2025 year-end and 2026-06-30 while last-twelve-months EBITDA rose by USD 312.64 million, so earnings growth absorbed only part of the added borrowing.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 10–12; calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-05; calculation CALC-06

Scores supplied USD 1,117.22 million of the USD 1,293.46 million of total segment operating income in the first nine months of fiscal 2026, so the debt service capacity rests mainly on one segment whose revenue depends on the three consumer reporting agencies for 60% of total revenues.

Cash interest cover, EBITDA over interest actually paid, was 7.03x in fiscal 2024, 9.07x in fiscal 2025 and 7.60x on a last-twelve-months basis at 2026-06-30. Paid interest lags the new borrowing: the term loan was drawn on 2026-06-05, the 2026 senior notes were issued on 2026-03-20 with a 6.25% coupon, and the filing states weighted-average rates on the revolver and term loan that sit above the 4.00% coupon of the 2028 senior notes, so the cash cost of the larger stack is only partly in the paid figure.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 10–12; calculation CALC-03; calculation CALC-07
### Cash flow quality

Operating cash flow was USD 777.88 million in the first nine months of fiscal 2026 against USD 555.14 million a year earlier, while derived EBITDA rose to USD 1,011.27 million from USD 698.63 million, so the conversion of EBITDA into operating cash flow slipped as cash interest paid rose to USD 162.42 million from USD 101.11 million and cash taxes rose to USD 162.88 million from USD 129.08 million. Capital expenditures are small, USD 27.85 million in nine months, so nearly all operating cash flow is free cash flow.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 90–91; calculation CALC-02; calculation CALC-10

Repurchases of common stock were USD 3,045.99 million in cash in nine months against free cash flow of USD 750.04 million as the issuer states it, so the difference was funded largely by net borrowing: proceeds of USD 2,950.00 million from the revolver and term loans and USD 1,000.00 million from senior notes, less USD 1,015.00 million and USD 400.00 million repaid. The filing states that the term loan funded the accelerated repurchase and that the 2026 senior notes repaid the 2018 senior notes.
### Liquidity and debt structure

Cash was USD 248.44 million at 2026-06-30 and the revolver had USD 290.00 million of commitment not drawn, before any letters of credit, none of which the filings disclose, so liquidity on the filings' figures is USD 538.44 million against USD 859.14 million at the 2025 year-end. Scheduled term loan installments of USD 300.00 million fall due within twelve months, and the issuer states that cash, available revolver borrowings and operating cash flow are expected to cover them.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 33; calculation CALC-08; calculation CALC-09

Principal of USD 5,610.00 million at 2026-06-30 matures from fiscal 2026 to fiscal 2034, with USD 1,987.50 million due in fiscal 2028 when the remaining term loan balance and the 2028 senior notes fall together and USD 710.00 million of revolver borrowings falling due in fiscal 2030. USD 2,210.00 million of principal, the revolver and the term loan, is floating-rate. The revolver and term loan are described as unsecured and the note indentures as carrying covenants typical of unsecured obligations, but no source states legal ranking, guarantors or co-issuers.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 10–12; calculation CALC-11; calculation CALC-04
### Definitions, funding float and later events

Deferred revenue of USD 205.42 million at 2026-06-30, USD 187.37 million at 2025-09-30 and USD 156.90 million at 2024-09-30 is billed ahead of recognition and funds operations without interest, so it is working-capital float rather than ordinary payables, and a slowdown in new software bookings could reverse it.

The sources state no subsequent event after 2026-06-30 that changes net debt. The settlement of the accelerated share repurchase is expected in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 and delivers shares against the USD 300.00 million already prepaid, so it does not change debt, and the first term loan installment of USD 75.00 million is due on 2026-09-30. The nine-month repurchase amount has two figures, USD 3,045.99 million paid in cash and USD 3,052.89 million recorded in equity, and each is used for its own purpose.
### Contrary evidence and monitoring

The strongest contrary evidence is earnings quality at the Scores segment, where segment operating income was 90% of segment revenue in nine months, and free cash flow of USD 750.04 million in the same period, which together would support debt reduction if repurchases slowed. The covenant definition could also add back share-based compensation of USD 174.29 million over twelve months and report a lower ratio than the derived one. The view would change on the executed credit agreement's definition, on the fiscal 2026 results and on the interest cost of the new borrowings once a full period is reported.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Fair Isaac is a high-margin scoring franchise that depends on three distributors, and its board has chosen to fund very large share repurchases with new borrowing, so financial policy is the main risk for creditors, ahead of business risk.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 15; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_exhibit991erq32026.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation CALC-02; calculation CALC-03

Scores produced 66% of nine-month revenue at a 90% segment margin, but its growth leaned on a higher mortgage score unit price, and three consumer reporting agencies paid 63% of third-quarter revenue. Total debt rose USD 2,526.70 million in nine months as repurchases of USD 3,045.99 million reached 4.06x free cash flow of USD 750.04 million, and no sponsor or controlling holder is established to support equity. Governance and financial-policy risk is medium, moving toward high if borrowing-funded repurchases continue as the leverage covenant ceiling, raised from 3.5x to 4.5x by the June 2026 amendment, steps back to 4.0x on 2026-12-31 and 3.5x on 2027-12-31.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 32–33; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_exhibit991erq32026.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation CALC-02; calculation CALC-03
### Key findings

Scores is the credit, and it is performing: it produced 66% of nine-month revenue at a 90% segment margin and 95% of the nine-month revenue increase, so earnings quality is high but rests on one product line. Operating cash flow was USD 777.88 million for nine months and capital spending was only 1.48% of revenue, so cash conversion is not the constraint.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 32–33; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-08

Concentration among distributors is rising and is, in our view, the largest business risk. Experian, TransUnion and Equifax together paid 63% of third-quarter revenue, up from 51% in fiscal 2025 and 41% in fiscal 2023, and they established VantageScore, a joint venture that sells a competing score. These distributors can ask to change the terms on which they offer the FICO Score, and the company says it has limited visibility until their royalty reports arrive, so a change in one relationship would reach the highest-margin revenue first.

Growth in Scores leans on price, which can reverse. The company attributes the third-quarter business-to-business increase to a higher mortgage origination scores unit price, its risk factors warn that limits on score fees could constrain further price increases, and the Federal Housing Finance Agency director announced in July 2025 that mortgage originators may choose the credit score they submit to Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac. A price or policy reversal would fall almost directly to profit because the segment's costs are small, which is our interpretation of its 91% third-quarter margin.

Software diversifies the business only slowly. Third-quarter software revenue rose 2%, and annual recurring revenue grew 10% to USD 815.8 million because platform products grew 62% while non-platform recurring revenue fell 17% with net retention of 82%. Segment margin fell to 26% from 32% as point-in-time licence sales declined and hosting costs rose.

Financial policy is the binding risk. Between June 2025 and June 2026 the board approved three successive repurchase programmes, each larger than the last, and nine-month repurchases of USD 3,045.99 million were 4.06x free cash flow of USD 750.04 million, so lenders and noteholders funded the gap. The USD 1.5 billion accelerated repurchase was paid on the day the USD 1.5 billion term loan was drawn, and total liabilities of USD 6,134.51 million are now 3.01x total assets of USD 2,037.37 million.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 4; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_exhibit991erq32026.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation CALC-03; calculation CALC-05; calculation CALC-07

Governance is only partly evidenced, and no sponsor or controlling holder is established, so there is no identified party to inject equity or cure a covenant breach. Board composition, committees, ownership and related-party dealings sit in a proxy statement that was not supplied, which leaves the board's alignment with creditors to be judged from its recorded actions, and those actions include the borrowing-funded repurchases described above.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 131–132; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 1; Source readiness (CP-0)

A surviving antitrust claim is a live but unquantified risk. The Sherman Act Section 2 claim and accompanying state law claims against the company continue through discovery after the court dismissed all other claims on 2024-11-24, and the filings state no material exposure for matters with a reasonable possibility of loss and give no estimate. An adverse outcome could reach the pricing and distribution practices behind Scores growth, which is an analyst interpretation.

Disclosure is adequate on terms but thin on risk. The quarterly reports state each debt instrument, the leverage covenant steps and covenant compliance, but the annual risk factors contain no stand-alone risk factor on the company's own indebtedness, and the third-quarter report says risk factors had no material changes although total debt had risen by USD 2,526.70 million since the year-end.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 10–12; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 32–56; calculation CALC-02
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a cautious view is cash generation and market access. Free cash flow was USD 750.04 million in nine months, the Scores margin reached 91% in the third quarter, capital spending is light, and the company placed USD 1.5 billion of senior notes in May 2025 and USD 1.0 billion in March 2026 while the disclosed fair value of its senior notes was 98.04% of face value on 2026-06-30. The revolving line runs to 2030-05-13, covenant compliance is reported, no cash dividend has been paid since May 2017, and the filings record no priming, uptier or other action against existing lenders. Repurchase programmes are open-ended authorisations, not commitments, so the board can slow them at any time; only the accelerated repurchase is contractually fixed.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-07-29_exhibit991erq32026.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 61; calculation CALC-06

Risk would fall if the board commits repurchases to free cash flow, states a leverage target, or the proxy statement shows a stable holder base and independent oversight of financial policy. It would rise if repurchases again exceed free cash flow after the covenant ceiling steps down to 4.0x on 2026-12-31, if the board starts a further programme funded by borrowing, if a consumer reporting agency or the federal housing regulator changes how the FICO Score is priced or used in mortgages, or if the antitrust claim produces a remedy that touches score pricing.
### Limitations

- The 2026 proxy statement is not available, so shareholder concentration, board independence, committee oversight and related-party dealings are not established. This limits the conclusion that no controlling holder exists and could change the governance rating if a large holder or a related-party arrangement appears.
Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 131–132; Source readiness (CP-0)

- The credit agreement and note indentures are not available, so restricted-payment capacity, guarantor structure and the covenant's definition of earnings are not established. The conclusion that financial policy rather than legal capacity drives the risk rests on observed behaviour and could change if the documents cap repurchases or add guarantees.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; Source readiness (CP-0)

- The terms of the distribution agreements with the three consumer reporting agencies (price schedules, term, renewal and termination rights) are not disclosed, so the durability of price-led Scores growth cannot be measured and confidence in the revenue durability view is reduced.

- The latest evidence is dated 2026-06-30, so settlement of the accelerated share repurchase and any repurchases or borrowing since then are not known. The conclusion on borrowing-funded repurchases could be out of date by the as-of date.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 13
- The content of the March 2026 charter amendment is not stated in the supplied filings, so the assessment of control and takeover defences may omit a change made that month.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-03-31_fico-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 43

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

In fiscal 2026 the company took two large financing steps. On 2026-03-20 it issued USD 1.0 billion of 6.25% senior notes due 2034 and used the proceeds to make a payment against the revolving line and to repay in full, before its May 2026 maturity, the USD 400.0 million 5.25% notes. On 2026-06-05 it borrowed a USD 1.5 billion unsecured term loan maturing 2028-05-15 under an amended credit agreement and paid USD 1.5 billion the same day to Wells Fargo Securities under an accelerated share repurchase, receiving an initial 1,055,103 shares worth about USD 1.2 billion and prepaying USD 300.0 million for shares to be delivered when the agreement settles, expected in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026.

In fiscal 2025 the company issued USD 1.5 billion of 6.00% senior notes due 2033 on 2025-05-13, used the proceeds to repay its USD 300 million and USD 450 million term loans, and amended the credit agreement to lift the revolving line from USD 600 million to USD 1.0 billion with its maturity extended to 2030-05-13. Total debt at carrying value was USD 3,055.69 million at 2025-09-30 and USD 5,582.39 million at 2026-06-30, and the revolving line was drawn USD 710.0 million at the later date.

No acquisition appears in the cash flow statements for fiscal 2023 to 2025 or for the nine months of fiscal 2026. The only disposal was the sale of certain assets of the Siron compliance business in fiscal 2023, with a gain of USD 1.9 million, and the only restructuring was the elimination of 226 positions in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025 at a cost of USD 10.9 million. The credit agreement permits borrowings for acquisitions and share repurchases, and the leverage covenant allows a step up to 4.0x after certain permitted acquisitions, so acquisition capacity exists but no acquisition appetite is evidenced.

# Fundamental credit: FAIR ISAAC CORP
## Request

FAIR ISAAC CORP (issuer id fico), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway: assess the issuer's fundamental credit profile, its strongest support and primary downside path, and the monitoring signals that matter to creditors. The analysis rests on the seven supplied filings and releases dated to 2026-07-29 and on the earlier Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance analyses.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Fair Isaac pairs a highly profitable, cash-generative scoring franchise with derived gross leverage that rose to 4.46x in nine months of borrowing-funded repurchases, so creditors depend on mortgage score pricing holding and on the board slowing repurchases.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 26; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-09

Free cash flow was USD 960.88 million over twelve months against cash interest paid of USD 164.87 million, but interest at the rates now in place is about USD 316.51 million a year, which would take cover from 7.60x to 3.96x. If the nine-month rise in Scores earnings reversed, derived leverage would reach 6.28x while cash after interest, tax and capital spending would still cover the USD 300.00 million of term loan installments due within twelve months, so a covenant test would come under pressure before liquidity. Fundamental credit quality is adequate: strong on cash conversion, weak on financial policy.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 32–33; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-02; calculation CALC-03; calculation CALC-05; calculation CALC-06
### Key findings

The scoring franchise earns very high margins and turns almost all of them into cash. Derived EBITDA was USD 1,252.44 million over twelve months, 52.32% of revenue, and free cash flow was USD 960.88 million, 76.72% of EBITDA. Scores segment margin was 90% for nine months and capital spending only 1.48% of revenue, so a revenue loss falls to profit but reinvestment takes little cash.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 32–33; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_exhibit991erq32026.htm.jsonl, page 5; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-08

Leverage is the weakest dimension and policy, not operations, set it. Derived gross leverage rose to 4.46x from 3.25x at the 2025 year-end and net leverage to 4.26x from 3.11x, because total debt rose USD 2,526.70 million while derived EBITDA rose USD 312.64 million. Cash repurchases of USD 3,045.99 million were 4.06x free cash flow of USD 750.04 million in the nine months.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 10; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_exhibit991erq32026.htm.jsonl, page 5; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-09; calculation CALC-11

Interest will take more of the cash flow than the latest cover shows. Cover on interest actually paid was 7.60x, but the coupons and floating rates stated at 2026-06-30 imply about USD 316.51 million a year against USD 164.87 million paid over twelve months, so cover on current rates is 3.96x. USD 2,210.00 million of the debt floats, and the filings disclose no interest rate hedge.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 41; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-02; calculation CALC-03; calculation CALC-07

Concentration and price dependence are the main business risk. Scores produced 86.37% of nine-month segment operating income, three consumer reporting agencies paid 63% of third-quarter revenue, and management attributes the Scores increase to a higher mortgage score unit price, with higher volume also contributing in the nine months, so earnings are exposed to a pricing or policy decision the company does not control.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 32–33; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 46; calculation CALC-04

Software is not yet an offset. Segment margin was 28% for nine months against 31% a year earlier and segment operating income fell 8%, while recurring revenue rose 10% only because platform products grew 62% against a 17% fall in non-platform products with net retention of 82%.

Liquidity is adequate for twelve months but thinner than a year ago, and the maturity wall is in fiscal 2028. Cash of USD 248.44 million plus USD 290.00 million of undrawn revolver, before letters of credit, gives USD 538.44 million against USD 859.14 million at the 2025 year-end and USD 300.00 million of term loan installments due within twelve months, while USD 1,987.50 million falls due in fiscal 2028.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 33; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Governance does not offset the leverage. No sponsor or controlling holder is established to support equity, the board approved three successively larger repurchase programmes between June 2025 and June 2026, and Business & governance rates governance and financial-policy risk medium, moving toward high if borrowing-funded repurchases continue.

In a Scores downturn the covenant, not cash, is the first break point. Reversing the nine-month Scores gain would cut derived EBITDA to USD 888.68 million and lift derived gross leverage to 6.28x against stated ceilings of 4.5x, 4.0x and 3.5x, whereas USD 400.83 million of cash after interest, tax and capital spending would still cover the USD 300.00 million of installments. The covenant's own earnings definition is not supplied, so headroom is not calculable.

### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence for a better view is that the leverage is a choice. Free cash flow of USD 960.88 million over twelve months, applied entirely to debt, would cut derived gross leverage from 4.46x to 3.69x, the board can slow repurchases at will, and the company reports covenant compliance, placed USD 1.5 billion of senior notes in May 2025 and USD 1.0 billion in March 2026, and has senior notes whose disclosed fair value was 98.04% of face value at 2026-06-30. The first scheduled principal payments are small and the largest maturity is in fiscal 2028.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 104; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-07; calculation CALC-10

The view would improve if the board stated a leverage target or limited repurchases to free cash flow, if the executed credit agreement showed covenant headroom on its own definition, or if the platform migration lifted Software margin toward its fiscal 2025 level of 30%. It would worsen if repurchases again exceeded free cash flow after the ceiling steps down to 4.0x on 2026-12-31, if the housing regulator or a consumer reporting agency changed how the FICO Score is priced or used in mortgages, if floating rates rose, or if Scores revenue fell.

### Strengths and weaknesses

Strength: Scores profitability and cash conversion. Scores segment margin was 90% for nine months and 91% in the third quarter, derived EBITDA margin was 52.32% over twelve months and capital spending was 1.48% of revenue, so free cash flow of USD 960.88 million covers interest and scheduled amortisation several times and could delever the company quickly if repurchases stopped.

Strength: a staggered, mostly fixed-rate unsecured maturity profile with proven market access. The notes mature in 2028, 2033 and 2034, the revolver in 2030, USD 2.5 billion of notes was placed between May 2025 and March 2026, and the disclosed fair value of the notes was 98.04% of face value, so refinancing pressure before fiscal 2028 is limited.

Strength: Software recurring revenue is shifting to a platform with high retention. Platform recurring revenue grew 62% to USD 412.8 million with net retention of 148%, and remaining performance obligations were USD 680.4 million, which adds contracted visibility to a segment that is otherwise a small part of profit.

Weakness: borrowing-funded repurchases. Derived gross leverage rose to 4.46x from 3.25x in nine months, cash repurchases were 4.06x free cash flow, and the covenant ceiling reported after the June 2026 amendment that added the term loan is 4.5x against 3.5x before, so the board has shown a willingness to use leverage capacity for shareholders.

### Business and ownership assessment

Fair Isaac is a US analytics software company whose profit comes mainly from Scores, a usage-based royalty on credit scores generated through consumer reporting agencies, with Software as the smaller and slower segment. This supports cash-flow visibility in activity terms but not in price terms: royalties arrive after each billing period and depend on mortgage and credit card volumes, so debt service capacity rests on activity the company does not control. Financial services supplied 92% of fiscal 2025 revenue, and revenue was USD 2,393.58 million over the last twelve months.

Basis: 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 53; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Ownership gives creditors no sponsor to lean on. The supplied documents identify no controlling holder, the proxy statement with board and ownership detail was not supplied, and the board approved three successively larger repurchase programmes between June 2025 and June 2026. Business & governance rates governance and financial-policy risk medium, moving toward high. The group is one registrant with unnamed consolidated subsidiaries and no stated guarantors, so the priority of the unsecured debt within the group is not established.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 35–36; 10-K_2025-09-30_fico-20250930.htm.jsonl, pages 131–132
### Revenue durability and pricing power

Revenue is recurring in Software and usage-based in Scores, and neither is locked in for a creditor's horizon. Software recurring revenue was USD 815.8 million at 2026-06-30 and remaining performance obligations were USD 680.4 million, about half due within 14 months, which gives visibility. Scores royalties give none because distributors report volumes after the period. Pricing power is evident, since the third-quarter business-to-business increase was attributed to a higher mortgage origination scores unit price, but three consumer reporting agencies paid 63% of quarterly revenue, they sell a competing score, and the company's own risk factors say fee limits or a regulator's score-choice decision could constrain price. Price, concentration and policy risk are one risk, so revenue is predictable in Software and cyclical, concentrated and exposed to substitution in Scores.
### Margin resilience and cost flexibility

Margins are high and hard to erode through costs but can fall sharply on revenue. Scores segment costs were 10% of segment revenue for nine months, so lost price or volume falls almost entirely to operating income, while Software segment margin fell to 28% from 31% as point-in-time licence sales declined and third-party hosting costs rose. Operating expenses were 47% of revenue, with personnel and hosting the main increases, and 226 positions were removed in fiscal 2025, so cost action is available. Margins can be defended against modest volume pressure but not against a loss of Scores price.
### Cash conversion and capital intensity

Nearly all EBITDA reaches free cash flow before debt repayment: free cash flow was 76.72% of derived EBITDA over twelve months, and capital spending was 1.48% of nine-month revenue. Deferred revenue is customer-funded float rather than payables, and a slowdown in new software bookings could reverse it. Cash interest is the growing leakage, rising from USD 103.56 million in fiscal 2025 to USD 164.87 million over twelve months, and conversion slipped from 78.68% to 76.72% as it rose, with a full year of the new debt still to come.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-07-29_exhibit991erq32026.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 4; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-01; calculation CALC-08
### Industry forces

Rivalry is intense in Software and concentrated in Scores. In Software the company names fraud, origination and decisioning competitors such as Nice Actimize, Experian, Pegasystems and SAS and says many competitors are larger. In Scores the one scaled rival is VantageScore, a joint venture of the same three agencies that distribute the FICO Score. Entry is hard because the company holds no consumer credit data of its own and scores are built on agency files, but the housing regulator's validation process lets lenders use other models. Substitutes are in-house models and alternative scores, so price is the lever that most invites substitution, which is an analyst interpretation.

Buyer power is high: customers are mostly large banks, insurers and agencies, many larger than the company, that can demand lower prices and non-standard terms, and the three agencies are at once buyers and competitors. Supplier power is moderate: the agencies supply the data behind the scores and distribute them, and third-party cloud and data-centre hosting is a rising cost that management cites for the fall in Software margin.
### Regulatory and macro factors

Regulatory and economic factors are material to credit, while social and technology factors are not a primary driver on the supplied materials. Use of the FICO Score for mortgages sold to Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac is subject to ongoing validation by those enterprises and their regulator, whose director announced in July 2025 that originators may choose the credit score they submit, and legislative or regulatory limits on score fees could constrain price increases. The company is also subject to consumer-protection supervision and, for products using artificial intelligence, to the European Union's AI Act, which takes effect mostly in 2026.

Economic exposure is direct: banking supplied 92% of fiscal 2025 revenue, and Scores volumes depend on mortgage and credit card activity, which falls when credit tightens or rates rise. Higher rates also raise the cost of the USD 2,210.00 million of floating-rate debt by about USD 22.10 million a year for each percentage point, so a rate rise that lowers mortgage volume would hit both sides of the cash flow.

### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next twelve to twenty-four months management guides fiscal 2026 revenue of USD 2.53 billion, up from USD 2.45 billion in earlier guidance, and the near-term path for creditors is set by whether repurchases slow before the ceiling steps down to 4.0x on 2026-12-31. The first term loan installment of USD 75.00 million is due on 2026-09-30, and installments of USD 300.00 million fall within twelve months. The medium-term outlook of three to five years is not established because no multi-year guidance, rating or market view is supplied.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-07-29_exhibit991erq32026.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 33; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Company-specific tailwinds are the Scores unit price, platform growth of 62% and net retention of 148%, and free cash flow; headwinds are non-platform runoff of 17%, hosting cost, higher interest cost and the covenant path. Sector tailwinds are not evidenced beyond mortgage and credit card activity, and the sector headwind is regulatory and competitive pressure on score pricing.
### Downside scenario

The issuer-specific downside begins with a pricing or policy event in mortgage scores, for example score choice moving volume to a competing score or a distributor winning a lower price. The first operational break is Scores revenue: segment costs are small, so the nine-month increase in Scores segment operating income of USD 363.76 million would reverse almost one for one, taking derived EBITDA from USD 1,252.44 million to USD 888.68 million. Derived gross leverage would reach 6.28x, net leverage 6.00x and, even if share-based compensation of USD 174.29 million were added back, 5.25x, against stated ceilings of 4.5x, 4.0x and 3.5x. A reversal of only half the increase gives 5.21x.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 32–33; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-05

Liquidity is the second step and holds. After run-rate interest of USD 316.51 million, tax at the nine-month rate and capital spending, about USD 400.83 million of cash would remain against USD 300.00 million of term loan installments, with USD 290.00 million of undrawn revolver and repurchases as a lever. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid a liquidity crisis, but a covenant test on a definition not supplied would be the first constraint, and an amendment of the kind agreed in June 2026 could be needed before the ceiling falls to 4.0x. This is an illustration of mechanics, not a forecast or a default view.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 16; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation CALC-02; calculation CALC-06
### Overall credit view

Overall, Fair Isaac presents a strong business profile supported by a 90% Scores margin and free cash flow of USD 960.88 million, but credit quality is constrained by derived gross leverage of 4.46x built through borrowing-funded repurchases. Cash-flow durability appears adequate: conversion is high, but it depends on mortgage score price and three distributors. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on repurchases slowing, on the covenant definition and on continued market access before the fiscal 2028 maturities of USD 1,987.50 million. The primary downside path is a pricing or policy change that reduces Scores earnings while interest and the covenant ceiling tighten. Against typical leveraged-credit issuers the profile is stronger on margin and cash conversion and weaker on leverage, but that comparison is qualitative because no peer data is supplied. Further analysis would require the executed credit agreement, the price and volume split of Scores growth and market evidence. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: borrowing-funded repurchases against a concentrated earnings base.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_fico-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 32–33; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation CALC-03; calculation CALC-05
